items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: if they came to Washington, they came up to Freddy Woods' place.

ctx.x: recorded. And a lot of those tunes, Lester when he came down here would have just come from New York, and they'd just tunes. He would sit there, and he would ask if I knew this or this, and I'd say "No" -- he would teach it to me right there.

All of this was in this learning process of me meeting some of the greatest musicians in the world, and a lot of times not even being aware of just really how great they were! But all these people used to come...if they came to Washington, they came up to Freddy Woods' place.

Toby Walker, if I can go back to him, was a fabulous pianist. They had a thing, it was sort of a phenomenon I guess you'd call it, that people would come far and wide and give him five dollars to play George Gershwin's "I Got Rhythm" very fast, and play it for an hour himself. And many times I walked in the club there, and he had this very fast striding left hand, and people would be all around...he would be going through one of these hours. And as I said, if someone gave him five dollars, that meant that a lot…
